title: Relative smooth SNC resolution of a tame semilinear quotient
statement: Let $F$ be a field and $K/F$ a finite separable field extension [def-weil-field] [def-pc-field-extension]. Let $H$ be a finite group of order invertible in $F$, acting on $K$ by $F$-automorphisms. Let $Y$ be a smooth projective $K$-scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-kun-projective] with an action of $H$ by $F$-scheme automorphisms, equivariantly for $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $D\subseteq Y$ be an invariant reduced relative strict normal crossings divisor over $K$ [def-trf-smooth-strict-normal-crossings-divisor]: it is effective Cartier, has finitely many distinct integral components, and the intersection of any $r$ distinct components is empty or smooth over $K$ of pure codimension $r$. Suppose $q:Y\to Q=Y/H$ is the finite categorical geometric scheme quotient, with orbit geometric fibres and invariant structure sheaf [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. There are a smooth projective $F$-scheme $R$ and a projective surjective morphism $v:R\to Q$ [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism] which is an isomorphism on a dense open meeting every component of $Q$, and induces a bijection of irreducible-component generic points and equality of their residue fields [def-weil-irreducible-components] [def-sc-generic-point] [def-weil-residue-field]. The reduced closed subscheme with support $v^{-1}(q(|D|))$ is a relative strict normal crossings divisor on $R/F$. Its irreducible components are smooth over $F$, and every intersection of $r$ distinct components is empty or smooth over $F$ of pure codimension $r$. Locally on $R$ the components through a point have equations which are distinct members of a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]; thus the same reduced divisor is a strict normal crossings boundary on the regular scheme $R$ [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Disconnected $Y$, a nonfaithful action on $Y$ or $K$, and the empty divisor are allowed. Projective over a field means admitting a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over that field. Field-extension terminology and degrees are as in [def-pc-field-tower].

source.place: Expose X Theorem 1.1, printed pp.135--136, and 2.3 Step 3, pp.151--152: component stabilizers modulo generic inertia, orbit induction, projective log modification of the quotient and saturated monoidal resolution (VIII 3.4.9); the trivial-base log chart from X 1.2 gives relative smoothness. Strictification and parameter/intersection criterion: VIII 4.1.2--4.1.8 and 4.2.2(i), pp.117--118. Boundary is the inverse image of the image of the original divisor, not the whole auxiliary enlarged boundary.
